scope: Stable local signing preparation; no keychain, certificate, trust, OS setting, or Swift build mutations performed by the implementer
status: installed and signed native owner/TCC acceptance verified by main

sources.findings: A stable designated requirement identifies updates independently of certificate authority type. Self-signed identities are supported; an OpenSSL code-signing certificate creation procedure is provided. Certificate leaf SHA-1 and identifier are supported requirement constraints. Trust policies are subsystem specific.
Keychain Access Certificate Assistant supports self-signed certificates and configurable extensions; RSA must be at least 2048 bits.

sources.source: Installed macOS security help add-trusted-cert, security help import, and codesign man page
sources.findings: add-trusted-cert defaults to the user trust store; -p codeSign restricts trust policy, -d would select admin store and is omitted. import -x makes the imported private key nonextractable, -T restricts access to the named application; -A is deliberately omitted. codesign accepts certificate SHA-1 identity selection and -R tests an explicit requirement.

changes: Resolve signing identity before building or replacing the existing app; use the same resolved SHA-1 hash for all signatures and LoomOwnerRequirement.
Prefer exact local name Loom Dev Code Signing, then preserve existing Apple identity fallback; explicit LOOM_CODESIGN_IDENTITY accepts exact name, case-insensitive SHA-1, or '-'.
Require exactly one matching certificate hash; duplicated copies of the same certificate are deduplicated, distinct certificates with the same requested name fail.
Verify the final app against the sealed certificate leaf and identifier owner requirement.
implementation.repeatability: Once the uniquely named local identity is installed, bare scripts/package-dev-app.sh selects it before other Apple identities. For fail-closed builds use the explicit installed SHA-1; without an explicit selection and without a local or Apple identity, the existing warned ad-hoc fallback remains.

commands:
cat > "$signing_tmp/cert.cnf" <<'CONFIG'
[req]
distinguished_name=dn
x509_extensions=code_sign
prompt=no
[dn]
CN=Loom Dev Code Signing
[code_sign]
basicConstraints=critical,CA:false
keyUsage=critical,digitalSignature
extendedKeyUsage=critical,codeSigning
CONFIG
installation_plan_main_only.constraints: Run once after checking no such identity exists; do not regenerate on rebuild. The temp directory and private key must never be copied into the repo or printed. Scope remains user-only codeSign trust; no admin/system trust, SSL trust, Gatekeeper changes, or TCC resets. Import may ask for keychain/user authorization. Commands use installed OpenSSL 3.6.4; they were prepared but not executed by implementer.

verified: Nine isolated zsh selection behavior cases: preferred local identity, Apple fallback, explicit lowercase hash, exact name, missing identity rejection, distinct same-name rejection, duplicate same-certificate deduplication, no-identity ad-hoc fallback, explicit ad-hoc. Final harness 9/9 passed.
security find-identity -v -p codesigning before installation: 0 valid identities found.
checks.failed_then_fixed: Initial selection harness exposed zsh command-substitution newline collapse for two matches. Resolve to a scalar first and split with (f); the final ambiguity case now fails as required. Main subsequently reported OpenSSL 3 default PKCS8 private-key PEM was rejected by security import -f openssl; installation recipe now converts that same key to traditional RSA PEM before import.
unverified: Certificate generation/import/user trust and codesign actual private-key access; main owns these mutations.
Real signed app and host designated requirements, owner positive/negative checks, two-build TCC continuity.
Swift build and tests: shared owner main, deliberately not run by this implementer.
checks.scope: Implementer preparation checks; historical unverified list resolved where recorded in mainInstallation

runtime_acceptance_plan: Install the identity once; read its SHA-1 using security find-identity. Package with explicit LOOM_CODESIGN_IDENTITY=<hash>.
Check codesign --verify --deep --strict --verbose=2 on the app; inspect codesign -d -r- on both app and Contents/Helpers/LoomRunHost.app and confirm certificate-based requirements without cdhash.

Read LoomOwnerRequirement with /usr/libexec/PlistBuddy -c 'Print :LoomOwnerRequirement' <host>/Contents/Info.plist. codesign --verify --strict -R=<owner> <app> must pass. An ad-hoc signed /bin/echo copy using identifier local.loom.desktop.dev must fail this requirement, proving identifier alone is insufficient. Use an external temp directory for this negative fixture.

Launch app and actual run host from the final package path, exercise access to Documents, and grant the one initial permission where required. Record app/host DRs, sealed owner requirement and binary hash A outside the repository.

Quit and verify no app/run hosts remain. Rebuild and repackage at the same final app path with the same certificate. Ensure A and B differ in signed code: if rebuilding identical sources produces identical CDhashes, main can temporarily modify CFBundleVersion in the external packaged app and host Info.plists, then re-sign inside out (host, app) with the same identity and runtime options. Compare CDhashes with codesign -d -vv; app/host DR and sealed owner requirement must remain identical. This external-package perturbation verifies permission stability for changed signed contents without touching shared source.

Launch B and repeat the identical app and actual run-host Documents access. Confirm access succeeds without a new permission prompt; record observation. DR equality alone does not prove TCC continuity. Do not reset TCC between A and B.
